**Finding: compliant (preferred position).**

The Agreement contains no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on AP:

- **Section 1 (p0001)** affirmatively disclaims exclusivity and preserves AP's freedom to monetise Inventory elsewhere: "Nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating an exclusive arrangement… This Agreement will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties."
- Targeted searches for compete/competing/competitor, exclusivity, first-look/right of first refusal, field-of-use, territory, minimum volume commitments, and "Customer shall not/will not" surfaced no restriction on the businesses AP may operate or the products or services it may buy or build.
- The only Customer-side prohibitions (**p0025**) are ordinary licence-scope terms directed at Kubient's own Service (no third-party access, no reverse engineering, no resale or service-bureau use). These bound how AP uses Kubient's platform, not AP's own business or its procurement of competing ad-tech, so they fall outside this rule and are not flagged.

No redline proposed; the clause sits at the preferred position rather than the fallback.
